directive.title: Directive (EU) 2019/882 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 April 2019 on the accessibility requirements for products and services

keyDates.label: Transposition deadline
keyDates.quote: Member States shall adopt and publish, by 28 June 2022, the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive.

keyDates.label: Application date
keyDates.quote: They shall apply those measures from 28 June 2025.
keyDates.note: This is the date the obligations began to bite for in-scope products and services.

keyDates.label: Article 4(8) derogation ends
keyDates.quote: Member States may decide to apply the measures regarding the obligations set out in Article 4(8) at the latest from 28 June 2027.

keyDates.label: Transitional period ends
keyDates.quote: Member States shall provide for a transitional period ending on 28 June 2030 during which service providers may continue to provide their services using products which were lawfully used by them to provide similar services before that date.

keyDates.label: First Commission report due
keyDates.quote: By 28 June 2030, and every five years thereafter, the Commission shall submit to the European Parliament, to the Council, to the European Economic and Social Committee and to the Committee of the Regions a report on the application of this Directive.
keyDates.note: This is why no official EU-wide compliance or enforcement dataset exists yet.

otherTransitionalRules.rule: Service contracts agreed before 28 June 2025 may continue without alteration until they expire, but no longer than five years from that date.

Self-service terminals lawfully used to provide services before 28 June 2025 may continue to be used until the end of their economically useful life, but no longer than 20 years after their entry into use.

transposition.caveat: These counts are the number of national instruments each Member State has communicated to the Commission, not a measure of implementation quality or completeness. A state with one consolidated act is not behind a state with fifty amendments; it reflects legislative drafting style. EUR-Lex states that Member States bear sole responsibility for this information and that it does not prejudge Commission verification of completeness and correctness.
transposition.latestChange: Since the previous count on 14 October 2026, France notified Décret n° 2026-883 of 23 September 2026 (Journal officiel, 24 September 2026). It adds the directive's definitions of economic operators to the Consumer Code and requires market surveillance authorities to give consumers, on request and in an accessible format, the conformity information supplied by manufacturers, importers and distributors.

enforcementDataStatus.explanation: There is no official EU-wide compliance or enforcement dataset for the European Accessibility Act, and there will not be one before 2030. Article 33(1) sets the first Commission report on the application of the Directive at 28 June 2030. Some national regulators now publish figures, but each covers one country or one sector, and many enforcement claims in vendor content could not be traced to a regulator or court. Anything on this subject should be sourced to a named national regulator or court, one country at a time. Traced to primary sources as of 31 October 2026: on 4 June 2026 the Tribunal judiciaire de Caen, in an interim first-instance order in a case brought by the associations ApiDV and Droit Pluriel, ordered Carrefour France to comply, under a penalty of 500 euros per day that starts six months after the order (about 4 December 2026). It also ordered Carrefour France to pay the associations 10,000 euros in provisional damages and 3,000 euros in costs, and said the site cannot be only slightly accessible. On 5 May 2026 the Tribunal judiciaire de Lille refused interim relief in a similar case against Auchan E-Commerce France; that was not a ruling on the merits, and the associations say they will appeal. On 24 March 2026 the Dutch regulator ACM, which tested about 100 of the largest Dutch online stores plus the largest telecom and energy providers, reported that 61% of the largest online stores are not digitally accessible, and warned that companies that fail to improve risk enforcement action. Dutch broadcaster NOS reported in June 2026 that ACM had visited ten large webshops and planned a new test three months later. On 11 March 2026 the European Commission sent additional reasoned opinions to Germany and Croatia over remaining transposition gaps. We found no monetary fine issued by a national regulator under an EAA transposition law as of 31 October 2026. That means none was found, not that none exists. The Caen payments go to the associations and are not a regulatory fine.
